answer: Bonded staking curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to commit collateral into an escrow trellis. Rather than letting unvetted bots wander through transactions, nodes lock crypto-assets that are slashed upon misbehavior. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locked capital and liquidity loss per identity, preventing clones from multiplying like yarrow. A key limitation is that capital barriers entrench wealthy actors while excluding underfunded honest agents.
